description: Golden Q&A for the synthetic IoT RMS delay spread dataset (data/sample/iot-delay-spread). All names are fictional.

items.question: What is the title of the delay spread research project?
items.answer: A Neural Network Model of RMS Delay Spread for Indoor Internet-of-Things Deployments
items.evidence: A Neural Network Model of RMS Delay Spread for Indoor Internet-of-Things Deployments

items.question: Who is the author of the RMS delay spread project and which institute are they from?
items.answer: Alex Morgan, Department of Electronics and Communication, Northbridge Institute of Technology, Riverton.
items.evidence: Author: Alex Morgan, Department of Electronics and Communication, Northbridge Institute of Technology

items.question: What does RMS delay spread describe?
items.answer: How much a transmitted signal is smeared in time by multipath reflections; it limits the symbol rate a link can support.
items.evidence: describes how much a transmitted signal is smeared in time by multipath reflections

items.question: What are the five inputs of the delay spread neural network?
items.answer: Transmitter-receiver distance, carrier frequency, antenna height, environment type, and the LOS/NLOS condition.
items.evidence: the transmitter-receiver distance, the carrier frequency, the antenna height, the environment type, and the line-of-sight or non-line-of-sight (LOS/NLOS) condition

items.question: Which probability distribution does the shadowing term follow?
items.answer: A log-normal distribution, found by maximum-likelihood estimation.
items.evidence: this shadowing term was found to follow a log-normal distribution

items.question: How much did the neural model reduce the prediction RMSE compared with the log-distance model?
items.answer: From 9.8 ns to 4.1 ns on the held-out test sites.
items.evidence: reduced the prediction RMSE from 9.8 ns to 4.1 ns

items.question: For which degree programme was the delay spread project done?
items.answer: A Master of Technology programme (final-year research project).
items.evidence: final-year research project of a Master of Technology programme

items.question: In which journal was the delay spread article published, and what is its ISSN?
items.answer: Journal of Applied Wireless Engineering, ISSN 2799-0417.
items.evidence: Journal of Applied Wireless Engineering, ISSN 2799-0417

items.question: Which volume and issue of the journal contains the delay spread article?
items.answer: Volume 14, Issue 3, March 2024.
items.evidence: Volume 14, Issue 3, March 2024

items.question: What is the impact factor of the Journal of Applied Wireless Engineering?
items.evidence: Journal impact factor: 4.21

items.question: Which society publishes the Journal of Applied Wireless Engineering?
items.answer: The Society for Wireless Systems Research.
items.evidence: of the Society for Wireless Systems Research

items.question: What is the DOI of the delay spread article?
When was the delay spread manuscript received and when was it accepted?
items.answer: Received 2 November 2023; accepted after revision on 9 February 2024.
items.evidence: Received: 2 November 2023

items.question: What kind of peer review did the delay spread article go through?
items.answer: Double-blind review by two reviewers.
items.evidence: Review process: double-blind, two reviewers

items.question: What mean RMS delay spread was measured at the warehouse site in NLOS conditions?
items.answer: 58.4 ns (std dev 11.2 ns) at 45 m, 2.4 GHz.

items.question: What was the mean RMS delay spread in the laboratory under LOS conditions at 5.8 GHz?
What is the floor area of the warehouse measurement site?
items.answer: 2400 square metres.
items.evidence: | S4 | Warehouse | 2400 | Steel frame |

items.question: How is measurement site S2 constructed?
items.answer: Brick walls; it is a long narrow corridor with metal doors.
items.evidence: | S2 | Corridor | 210 | Brick walls | Long narrow corridor, metal doors |

items.question: How many hidden neurons does the proposed delay spread network use?
items.answer: Eight hidden neurons.
items.evidence: one hidden layer of eight neurons and one output neuron

items.question: After how many epochs did training of the delay spread network stop?
items.answer: After 64 epochs, when validation error had not improved for 6 epochs.
items.evidence: Training stopped after 64 epochs

items.question: What R squared did the proposed neural network reach on the test sites?
items.evidence: | Neural network, 8 hidden neurons (proposed) | 4.1 | 0.93 |

items.question: What are the limitations of the delay spread model?
items.answer: Validated only for 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz and buildings up to 2,400 square metres; outdoor-to-indoor links and millimetre-wave frequencies are not covered.
items.evidence: validated only for the 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz bands and for buildings up to 2,400 square metres

items.question: How were the categorical inputs encoded for the delay spread network?
items.answer: One-hot encoded (continuous inputs scaled to -1 to 1).
items.evidence: Categorical inputs (environment type and LOS/NLOS condition) are one-hot encoded

items.question: What future work is planned for the delay spread model?
items.answer: Extend it to 60 GHz millimetre-wave links, add outdoor-to-indoor measurements, and deploy it inside a network planning tool.
items.evidence: Extend the model to 60 GHz millimetre-wave links

items.question: Why is a large delay spread a problem for IoT links?
items.answer: It forces lower data rates for IoT links.
items.evidence: Large delay spread forces lower data rates for IoT links

items.question: How many channel snapshots were collected in the measurement campaign?
items.answer: 3,985 channel snapshots across the five sites.
items.evidence: A total of 3,985 channel snapshots were collected across the five sites

items.question: Which sites were held out for testing the delay spread model?
items.answer: Sites S4 and S5 (S1, S2 and S3 were used for training and validation).
items.evidence: sites S4 and S5 were held out for testing

items.question: What software was used to build and train the delay spread network?
items.answer: Python with PyTorch, using a custom Levenberg-Marquardt optimiser.
items.evidence: trained in Python with PyTorch, using a custom Levenberg-Marquardt optimiser
